name: a2uiverse-catalog
description: The A2UIVerse catalog contracts (SPEC §9.1, task 11.2), versioned with the sdk that carries them: what a catalog package exposes (the export contract), what the client lends a loaded catalog (the host-module interface), what Stellify, the pack tool, writes and the marketplace, the registry and the client verify (the catalog artifact, whose descriptor is the JSON Schema beside this file), and the checks the registry and the marketplace share — the card's declaration read per A2UI version, two-directional coverage, entitlement, the app id — and the credential bar's terms, which the hub matches against every paint. The agent is described by its A2A AgentCard alone and nothing here describes one. Normative for every language projection; each projection's contract test asserts against this file.

cardRead.rule: A card's A2UI declaration is read per version across its capabilities.extensions. Entries whose URI is the v0.9 or the v0.9.1 extension URI count; an entry for a version the platform does not speak is passed over, not an error. Inside a counted entry the params are read flat, as the extension guide writes them, or keyed under v0.9 or v0.9.1, the whole-object shape, each object validated against the capabilities schema's version part and the root's required key not applied; the entry's URI decides the version, the key never retargets it; both keys in one entry union into that entry's set; a third version key beside a counted one is passed over; an object keyed under neither is an error. Two entries under one URI merge. An entry naming no ids says nothing about catalogs. One malformed entry fails the whole read, each error naming its entry's version. The map comes out filled: a version whose entries name no ids takes the other version's set, so only a card whose entries name different sets keeps a version axis. The hub advertises each version's set under its capabilities key and checks a paint against the set of the version it is stamped with; everywhere else the app's catalog ids are the union, v0.9's then v0.9.1's, each once. A card naming no ids under any counted entry declares nothing and falls back to the basic catalog.

exportContract.rule: A catalog package's entry exports CATALOG, a Catalog from @a2ui/web_core built for @a2ui/react's React catalog model; its id is the catalog id. Provider, when exported, is a React component taking children — the one Provider of SPEC §9.2, wrapping every fragment of the catalog; absent, a passthrough wraps them. Every other export is ignored.

0.14.0.rule: The client registers one object under the global before any artifact loads: its version, the module namespace of each specifier — the client's own instances — and loadStylesheet, which loads a stylesheet by URL once. An artifact reaches the host singletons only through it: Stellify, the pack tool, rewrites each import of a specifier to a read from the interface and each stylesheet import to a load through it, and refuses any other specifier under a host package. Keyed by the A2UI runtime release the host lends, the release of @a2ui/react and @a2ui/web_core; the client refuses at load an artifact built against one it does not lend.

artifact.rule: A directory of files served under one base URL: the descriptor, the catalog schema, one ESM entry, its stylesheets, its assets. The descriptor lists every other file with its hash; the entry and the schema are among them; a file not listed does not belong to the artifact. The schema's catalogId equals the descriptor's.

coverage.rule: Two-directional: every catalog id the card declares is handed at install or public; every artifact handed is an id the card declares. A card declaring no catalogs hands nothing and falls back to the basic catalog.

entitlement.rule: An app's entitlement is the ids handed at its install plus the public catalogs; the shell catalog is in no app's set. Fixed at install, changed only by install-over. The hub advertises to each agent its own entitlement as a2uiClientCapabilities.supportedCatalogIds, never the table, and refuses a paint outside it.

appId.rule: A slug chosen by the publisher, unique in the marketplace's index: lowercase ASCII letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter.

credentialBar.rule: No credential input is painted on the canvas. The hub matches the terms case-insensitively as whole words — names split at case changes and separators — against every paint's component types, property names, and the property values its painter's catalog declares as fixed options, never free text or the data model; a paint with one match is refused whole.
